title: A coordinate lowers fibre dimension over a dense principal open
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, with both $R$ and $S$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Fix an integer $d\ge1$. Suppose every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] of $\operatorname{Spec}(S)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ [def-pc-scheme] has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $d$. Then there exist $a\in S$ and $f\in R$ such that $f$ belongs to no minimal prime ideal of $R$ (a minimal prime is a prime ideal containing no strictly smaller prime ideal), and every fibre of the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(S_f)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_f[t])$ induced by $t\mapsto a/1$ has dimension at most $d-1$. Here $R_f=R[1/f]$ and $S_f=S[1/\varphi(f)]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and $R_f[t]$ is the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Empty spectra have dimension $-\infty$ and are allowed.
